title: Selection-tool drag-move inconsistently snaps shape back to original position (cannot move)
description:
USER-REPORTED, SEVERE (core interaction broken). Dragging a shape with the Selection tool to move it often fails: the shape snaps back to its original position and cannot be moved. Happens INCONSISTENTLY (a timing/render-race / stale-closure smell).

REPRO
- Select a shape with the Selection (arrow) tool.
- Drag it to a new position and release.
- Frequently the shape jumps back to (near) its original position instead of staying where dropped. Intermittent — depends on how fast you drag and on React render timing.

ROOT CAUSE — stale React-closure on the document (NOT free-transform/rotate; that is a separate task).
The drag pipeline is incremental: StageArea.onMouseMove (packages/authoring-ui/src/StageArea.tsx:2772-2888) calls onShapeMove(id, dx, dy) with SMALL incremental deltas and re-baselines startMouseX/Y to the current mouse after every move (StageArea.tsx:2887), so each onShapeMove is a delta relative to the previous one. The model is expected to ACCUMULATE these deltas.

Shell wires onShapeMove -> handleShapeMove (Shell.tsx:1200-1231) and onShapeMoveEnd -> handleShapeMoveEnd (Shell.tsx:1234-1240). Both, and the underlying withTimeline/withSceneTimeline/withSymbolTimeline helpers (Shell.tsx:693-739), build the next document from the React-SUBSCRIBED closure value 'doc' (useStore(documentStore, selectDoc), Shell.tsx:581) — NOT from the live store documentStore.getState().history.present.

Mechanism (the snap-back):
1. handleShapeMove calls replaceDoc(withTimeline((prev) => ...)). 'prev' is the closure doc's timeline (withSceneTimeline reads doc.scenes[idx].timeline and spreads ...doc — Shell.tsx:695-702), and the moved object's base position is read as obj.x+dx from that same closure doc (Shell.tsx:1222-1224).
2. replaceDoc updates the Zustand store synchronously, but the React-subscribed 'doc' (and therefore the handleShapeMove closure) only refreshes on the NEXT render. React batches/coalesces renders, so multiple mousemove events routinely fire against the SAME stale closure doc within one render frame (more likely on a fast drag).
3. While the closure is stale, every onShapeMove rebuilds the doc from the ORIGINAL base position plus only the latest tiny re-baselined delta — discarding all accumulated movement. The live store gets overwritten with a near-origin position => the shape appears to snap back. Inconsistent because it depends on how many mousemoves land between renders.
4. Same defect on commit: handleShapeMoveEnd calls commitDrag(dragStartDocRef.current, doc) with the closure 'doc' (Shell.tsx:1237). If the final mousemove fired after the last render, the closure doc is behind the store present, so the committed undo 'present' records a stale (reverted) position even if the live store was momentarily correct.

This is the exact stale-closure class documented in CLAUDE.md 'MCP agent stale-closure bug' (callbacks capture React state at registration; getDoc returning a pre-mutation snapshot; fix = read/write via a synchronously-updated ref / live store getState). The agent/JSFL/test bridges were migrated to documentStore.getState() (see Shell.tsx:551-554 comment 'replaces the old latestDocRef stale-closure workaround'), but the drag handlers were NOT migrated and still read 'doc' from the React closure.

REGRESSION VERDICT
Regression. All offending lines (withSceneTimeline Shell.tsx:695-704, handleShapeMove Shell.tsx:1205-1230, commitDrag call Shell.tsx:1237) blame to commit 4b4e4cf2 ('initial progress', 2026-06-09) — the Zustand documentStore migration that removed the old latestDocRef stale-closure workaround for bridges but left the drag handlers reading the React-closure 'doc'. The recent Flash 8 re-theme commits (149be18 / 6dfe678 / 51c5e3b, etc.) touched Shell.tsx but ONLY the zoom/scenes control strip and chrome styling (~lines 3290-3378), NOT the drag/commit/render path — so the re-theme is NOT the cause. Investigation HEAD: 539643080b3cbef1f993eb3e5acb6ad8cbbf7e86.

EXPECTED vs ACTUAL
- Expected: dragging a shape moves it and the new position persists in the model and across the next render; mouseup commits exactly the dropped position as one undo step.
- Actual: during fast/multi-event drags the move is discarded and the shape snaps back to (near) its original position; the committed position can also be stale.

FIX DIRECTION (matched to root cause)
- Stop reading 'doc' from the React closure in the drag path. Source the live present from documentStore.getState() (the present is history.present — selectDoc, store/documentStore.ts:60) inside handleShapeMove / handleShapeMoveEnd and the withTimeline helpers used by the drag, so each incremental onShapeMove accumulates on the freshest doc and commitDrag commits the true final position. Options: (a) compute the next doc with a store-functional updater that receives the live present, or (b) keep a useRef mirroring history.present updated synchronously on every replaceDoc/pushDoc (the documented MCP-bridge useRef fix) and have the drag handlers read/write through it. Either way, replaceDoc during the drag and commitDrag on mouseup must operate on the live store present, not the rendered snapshot.
- Keep StageArea's incremental delta + re-baseline contract unchanged; the fix is entirely in the Shell handler/state-source.

ACCEPTANCE
- A test (interaction/unit at the Shell-handler level, or e2e) that simulates a MULTI-EVENT drag of a shape with the Selection tool WITHOUT a render flush between mousemoves (i.e. several onShapeMove(dx,dy) deltas dispatched back-to-back), then onShapeMoveEnd, and asserts the committed displayObject x/y reflect the FULL accumulated delta AND persist across a subsequent render (the store present after re-render still holds the moved position, not the original). Must fail on current code (stale closure discards intermediate deltas) and pass after the fix.
- Do NOT use Playwright/Ruffle if port 1420 is held; a deterministic Shell/store-level reducer test reproducing the no-render-flush race is preferred and sufficient.

NOTE: scope is the SELECTION-tool drag-move-and-commit path only; the free-transform ROTATE bug is a separate task.
